description: A three-row, nine-panel composite of EBSD maps of a Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steel at three hot-rolling reductions. Rows are (a-c) grey band-contrast (BC) maps, (d-f) phase maps overlaid with grain-boundary maps, and (g-i) Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) maps; columns are (a, d, g) HR45, (b, e, h) HR68 and (c, f, i) HR82. Every panel carries a 100 µm scale bar; panel (c) additionally prints RD (vertical arrow) and ND (horizontal arrow). In (d-f) the FCC phase is light blue, black lines are grain boundaries with θ > 15°, and red lines are Σ3 (60°(111)) annealing-twin boundaries, with the colour key printed inside (f). The BC maps show progressive grain refinement and an increasing density of dark, elongated/streaky features from (a) to (c). Straight red twin lines are abundant inside the grains of (a, d) and become shorter, finer and more numerous in (b, e) and (c, f). The KAM maps use a 0°-5° rainbow colour bar: (g) is dominated by dark blue with only sparse green, whereas (h) and especially (i) contain markedly more green/cyan high-gradient regions, indicating that local strain concentration increases with hot-rolling reduction.

subfigures.description: Grey band-contrast (BC) EBSD map of sample HR45; equiaxed grains, 100 µm scale bar, with sparse dark streaky/black defects.
Grey BC EBSD map of sample HR68; visibly finer equiaxed grain structure than (a), 100 µm scale bar.
Grey BC EBSD map of sample HR82; finest grain structure of the three, with RD (up) and ND (right) direction arrows and a 100 µm scale bar.
Phase map of HR45: light-blue FCC phase with black grain boundaries (θ > 15°) and numerous straight red Σ3 (60°(111)) twin boundaries inside coarse grains; 100 µm scale bar.
Phase map of HR68: light-blue FCC phase, black high-angle boundaries and dense red Σ3 twin boundaries in a finer, more subdivided grain structure; 100 µm scale bar.

Phase map of HR82 with the same colour scheme plus the on-panel legend (light blue = FCC phases; black = grain boundaries with θ > 15°; red = Σ3 (60°(111)) grain boundaries); very dense black and red boundary network; 100 µm scale bar.
KAM map of HR45 with 0°-5° rainbow colour bar; overwhelmingly blue (low misorientation) with isolated green high-gradient spots; 100 µm scale bar.
KAM map of HR68 with the same 0°-5° colour bar; more green/cyan areas along boundaries than (g); 100 µm scale bar.
KAM map of HR82 with 0°-5° colour bar; the most extensive green/yellow high-orientation-gradient regions of the three samples; 100 µm scale bar.

observations.observation: The group is a 3 x 3 composite: rows are band-contrast maps (a-c), phase maps with grain boundaries (d-f) and KAM maps (g-i); columns correspond to HR45, HR68 and HR82.
Each of the nine panels contains a scale bar labelled 100 µm.
Only panel (c) prints orientation arrows, labelled RD (pointing up) and ND (pointing right).
The phase-map legend printed in panel (f) reads: light blue = FCC phases; black = grain boundaries with θ > 15°; red = Σ3 (60°(111)) grain boundaries.
The KAM colour bars in (g), (h) and (i) are labelled 0° at the blue end and 5° at the red end, i.e. the KAM angle ranges from 0° to 5°.
In the KAM maps the area fraction of green-to-red (high orientation gradient) regions increases in the order (g) HR45 < (h) HR68 < (i) HR82.
The band-contrast maps show decreasing apparent grain size and an increasing density of dark streaky features from (a) HR45 to (c) HR82.

The phase maps show straight red Σ3 (60°(111)) twin boundaries inside the blue FCC austenite grains in all three samples, with the boundary network becoming denser and the twin lamellae shorter from (d) to (f).

The caption states that black and red lines denote HAGBs with misorientation ≥ 15° and Σ3 (60°〈111〉) grain boundaries, respectively, and that areas with high orientation gradients indicate local strain concentration.
The citing text reports mean austenite grain sizes of about 45.11, 27.02 and 18.80 µm for HR45, HR68 and HR82 respectively.
The citing text reports mean effective grain sizes including annealing twin boundaries of about 21.82 µm, 11.55 µm and 7.02 µm for HR45, HR68 and HR82 respectively.
The citing text reports Σ3 twin-boundary fractions of 67%, 60% and 52% (by length relative to total grain-boundary length with misorientation > 15°) for HR45, HR68 and HR82 respectively.

The citing text states that the HR82 sample exhibited more areas with high orientation gradients than the other samples, indicating more prevalent local strain concentration with increasing hot-rolling reduction.

The citing text attributes the grain refinement with increasing rolling reduction to enhanced dynamic recrystallization (DRX) and possible particle-stimulated nucleation (PSN) from (Nb,Mo,W)C particles.
